# Article templates

## How-to

```markdown
# How to [accomplish the task]

[One sentence: what this guide covers and when to use it.]

## Before you start
- [What is needed]

## Steps
1. [Verb first. Exact path, for example Settings > Integrations > API keys.]
   You should see [result].
2. [Next step]

## Check that it worked
[How to confirm success]

## Common problems
- [Problem]: [fix]

## Related articles
- [Link]
```

## Troubleshooting

```markdown
# [What the user sees]

If you see [symptom], this article explains how to fix it.

## Symptoms
- [What the user observes, including exact error text]

## Cause
[Short, plain explanation]

## Solution
### Option 1: [most likely fix]
[Steps]
### Option 2: [alternative]
[Steps]

## Prevent it
[How to avoid it]

## Still having trouble?
[How to contact support]
```

Lead with symptoms, not causes: customers search for what they see.

## FAQ

```markdown
# [Question in the customer's words]

[Direct answer in 1 to 3 sentences.]

## Details
[Context or nuance]

## Related questions
- [Link]
```

If the answer needs a walkthrough, write a how-to instead.

## Known issue

```markdown
# Known issue: [short description]

Status: [Investigating / Workaround available / Fix in progress / Resolved]
Affected: [who or what]
Last updated: [date]

## Symptoms
[What users experience]

## Workaround
[Steps, or "No workaround yet"]

## Status of the fix
[Current status. Only an approved date, otherwise "We will update this article when we know more."]

## Updates
- [Date]: [update]
```

Keep status current. When the fix ships, mark it resolved and keep the article live for about 30 days.

## Maintenance

| Activity | How often |
| --- | --- |
| Review new articles before publishing | Every article (peer and subject-matter review) |
| Accuracy audit of top articles | Quarterly |
| Flag articles not updated in 6 months or more | Monthly |
| Update known-issue status | Weekly |
| Find top ticket topics without an article | Quarterly |

Update an existing article when the product changed or a detail is missing. Create a new one for a new feature, a gap found in tickets, or an article that covers too many topics.
